items.headline: Portugal picks Lufthansa to buy 44.9% of TAP for €1.025B
items.take: Portugal's government selected Lufthansa Group's offer of EUR 1.025 billion for a 44.9 percent stake in TAP Air Portugal, rising to up to EUR 1.2 billion for 49.9 percent; Lufthansa expects to sign the agreements shortly, with completion subject to regulatory approval. AlphaGen read: this gives Lufthansa a minority foothold in TAP's Atlantic network, and the regulatory reviews are the remaining gate.

items.headline: Siemens leads nine-figure round valuing Skeleton Technologies above $1B
items.take: Skeleton Technologies says a nine-figure round led by Siemens lifts its valuation above $1 billion; the money mainly funds U.S. manufacturing expansion, and the company plans to invest more than $200 million in scale-up and R&D in Silicon Valley. AlphaGen read: a strategic lead from Siemens links Skeleton's supercapacitor tech more tightly to data-center power demand, though the round size was not disclosed.

items.headline: Hulic tenders at ¥295 a share to take Riso Kyoiku private
items.take: Hulic, holder of 50.87% of Riso Kyoiku Group, launched a tender offer at 295 yen per share running October 14 to November 26, 2026, aiming to make the company a wholly owned subsidiary and delist it. AlphaGen read: it adds to the run of Japanese parent-subsidiary buyouts as groups simplify listed structures.
items.source_name: Riso Kyoiku Group tender offer announcement

items.headline: Nokia agrees to sell Enterprise Campus Edge unit to AURELIUS
items.take: Nokia signed a definitive agreement to sell its Enterprise Campus Edge private-wireless business, serving nearly 900 customers, to AURELIUS; terms were not disclosed and closing is expected in the first half of 2027. AlphaGen read: the carve-out continues Nokia's portfolio narrowing, moving a niche enterprise unit to a carve-out specialist.

items.headline: ECB's Schnabel to leave the Executive Board on Jan. 3, 2027 for an IMF role
items.take: The ECB's Governing Council agreed with its Ethics Committee on Sept. 24 that Isabel Schnabel's planned IMF role, starting Jan. 4, 2027, raised no conflict-of-interest concerns, so no cooling-off period applies; she resigned from the ECB effective Jan. 3, 2027, according to the Council's non-rate decisions published Oct. 2. The same release shows collateral and haircut guideline changes taking effect Nov. 30. Schnabel's exit opens one of the six Executive Board seats just as euro-area policy is wrestling with an energy-driven inflation shock, making the succession a policy story as much as a personnel one.
items.source_name: European Central Bank: Decisions taken by the Governing Council (2 October 2026)

items.headline: CBO pegs the FY2026 federal deficit at $2.0T, $218B wider than FY2025
items.take: The Congressional Budget Office estimates the fiscal 2026 deficit at $2.0 trillion, $218 billion more than in fiscal 2025. Revenues rose an estimated $169 billion, or 3%, while outlays climbed $386 billion, or 6%, led by net interest on the debt, major benefit programs, defense and education. With spending growth running at twice the pace of receipts and interest costs among the leaders, Treasury supply pressure on the long end is unlikely to ease into fiscal 2027.
items.source_name: Congressional Budget Office: Monthly Budget Review, September 2026

items.headline: CFTC seeks comment on rules for retail crypto trades and a 'crypto asset market'
items.take: The CFTC issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on 'Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions' and 'Regulation Crypto Asset Markets,' covering retail commodity transactions in crypto assets under section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act, including a proposed designated-contract-market subcategory called a 'crypto asset market.' Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication. An ANPRM is the earliest stage of rulemaking, but it signals the CFTC intends to build a dedicated venue framework for retail crypto spot-style trading rather than regulate it case by case.

items.headline: BoE flags gilt repo leverage; policy proposals due in early 2027
items.take: Bank of England executive director Nathanaël Benjamin said 'doing nothing is not an option' on gilt repo resilience and that 'out-of-control leverage is unwelcome,' with a comprehensive update and potential policy proposals planned for early 2027. He cited Bank research estimating that more central clearing could have cut gilt repo exposures on UK dealer balance sheets by 40% to 60% during the 2020 'dash for cash.' Central clearing and tighter haircuts would raise the cost of leveraged basis trades, a risk worth watching for hedge-fund demand at gilt and, by extension, Treasury auctions.
items.source_name: Bank of England: Speech by Nathanaël Benjamin (ISDA forum)

items.headline: BoE reserve balances slip £3.6B to £645.9B; short-term repo at £132.1B
items.take: Reserve balances at the Bank of England fell to £645.9 billion in the week to Oct. 14 from £649.6 billion a week earlier, while short-term repo lending eased to £132.1 billion from £133.4 billion, per the Bank's weekly report. The loan to the Asset Purchase Facility was unchanged at £521.8 billion. Repo usage of more than £130 billion shows banks are leaning steadily on Bank facilities as quantitative tightening drains reserves.
items.source_name: Bank of England Weekly Report, 14 October 2026

items.headline: Meta will report Q3 results after the close on Oct. 21
items.take: Meta Platforms said it will release third-quarter 2026 results after market close on Wednesday, Oct. 21, with a conference call at 4:30 p.m. ET. Its capital-spending commentary will be an early read on how large platforms are budgeting for AI infrastructure into 2027.

items.headline: Jio Platforms files IPO prospectus; all-primary issue of up to 270M shares
items.take: Jio Platforms' red herring prospectus dated October 14 covers a fresh issue of up to 270,000,000 equity shares with no offer for sale; anchor bidding is October 19 and the public issue runs October 21-23, with listing on BSE and NSE. AlphaGen read: with no selling shareholders, the offering is a pure capital raise for the company, and the size of the syndicate signals how much global distribution is being lined up.

items.headline: TKO goes public with $2.0B cash bid for Service Properties Trust hotels
items.take: TKO LLC said its October 7 letter of intent offers $2.0 billion in cash for SVC's hospitality portfolio, that it has had no meaningful response, and that it will put $50 million in escrow once SVC signs an NDA. AlphaGen read: it is an unsolicited, non-binding approach, so the next marker is whether SVC's board engages or discloses other bids.

items.headline: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II prices $100M shares-only SPAC IPO
items.take: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II sold 10,000,000 Class A shares at $10.00 for $100 million, with Nasdaq trading under TCXB from October 16 and no warrants or over-allotment option. AlphaGen read: dropping warrants trims dilution for a future healthcare target and reflects a cleaner SPAC structure.
items.source_name: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II press release (Business Wire)

items.headline: DSG to buy GradeEight for about $145M ahead of its own take-private
items.take: DSG's Lawson Products agreed to acquire GradeEight Holdings, with about $110 million in annual sales, for approximately $145 million, funded by revolver borrowings and cash, with closing expected in the fourth quarter. AlphaGen read: DSG keeps doing MRO bolt-ons while its going-private merger with LKCM Headwater affiliates is still pending.

items.headline: First Horizon swings to a Q3 loss of $0.20 a share on a $4.5B mortgage sale
items.take: First Horizon reported a third-quarter net loss available to common shareholders of $94 million, or $0.20 a diluted share, versus earnings of $0.50 a year earlier; excluding notable items of $0.73 a share, adjusted EPS was $0.53 versus $0.51. Net interest income (FTE) rose to $686 million from $678 million while the net interest margin slipped to 3.48% from 3.55%. The loss is an accounting reset rather than a credit event: the bank is taking the hit now to swap low-yielding mortgages for room to grow loans.
items.source_name: First Horizon Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: First Horizon books a $473M pretax loss to sell ~$4.5B of low-yield mortgages
items.take: First Horizon recorded a $473 million pretax loss in noninterest income (part of notable items totaling $347 million after tax), mainly from moving about $4.5 billion of lower-yielding consumer mortgages to held for sale; the bank says the sale will be accretive to earnings going forward. Period-end loans fell to $59.8 billion from $63.1 billion a year earlier, deposits rose to $67.7 billion from $65.5 billion, and preliminary CET1 was 10.3% versus 11.0%. With mortgage rates above 7%, regional banks still carrying loans written at much lower coupons face the same choice: hold them and accept thin spreads, or crystallize the loss and redeploy the capital.
items.source_name: First Horizon Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K, Ex. 99.1)
items.correction: Clarified that the $347 million after-tax figure is the total of all notable items, not the after-tax amount of the $473 million mortgage-sale loss alone.

items.headline: Warsh joins IMF's Georgieva for a Bangkok fireside chat at 11:30 p.m. ET tonight
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board calendar lists a discussion with Chairman Kevin Warsh at 11:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 15, a fireside chat with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva in Bangkok, Thailand. The Board's G.17 industrial production release follows at 9:15 a.m. on Oct. 16. Remarks this close to the Oct. 27–28 FOMC meeting will be read for how the Fed weighs the energy-driven jump in producer and consumer prices against slowing activity abroad.

items.headline: Proofpoint to buy Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3B
items.take: Proofpoint agreed to acquire Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3 billion, a 52% premium to Varonis' June 22 close before initial sale rumors and 17% above its September 1 close. Thoma Bravo committed equity and secured debt financing commitments, and closing is expected in the first half of 2027 subject to Varonis shareholder and regulatory approvals. The deal adds data-security software to Proofpoint's email and human-risk platform as private capital keeps consolidating listed security vendors.

items.headline: Nasdaq closes LeveL Markets buy, adding a top-three U.S. ATS
items.take: Nasdaq completed its acquisition of LeveL Markets, which it says is the third-largest U.S. alternative trading system by volume and processes hundreds of millions of shares daily across more than 7,000 symbols; terms were not disclosed. LeveL will keep running as a FINRA-registered ATS. Owning the venue gives Nasdaq a direct share of off-exchange equity flow.

items.headline: 26North to buy MEI Industrial Solutions from Olympus; terms undisclosed
items.take: 26North agreed to acquire MEI Industrial Solutions, a Dallas-based mover and installer of heavy equipment for data centers, semiconductor plants and other advanced manufacturing, from Olympus Partners; terms were not disclosed and closing is expected in Q4 2026. MEI has 30 operating locations and nearly 2,500 U.S. employees. The deal targets services capacity tied to the data-center build-out rather than the hardware itself.

items.headline: Interactive Brokers Q3 EPS rises to $0.69 as net interest income climbs 19%
items.take: Interactive Brokers reported Q3 GAAP diluted EPS of $0.69 versus $0.59 a year earlier, and $0.67 as adjusted versus $0.57, on reported net revenues of $1.91 billion versus $1.66 billion. Net interest income rose 19% to $1.15 billion, commissions rose 12% to $602 million and the pretax margin was 78%. The mix matters: with net interest income nearly double commissions, results lean more on client cash and margin balances than on trading volume.

items.headline: J.B. Hunt Q3 revenue rises 20% to $3.68B; diluted EPS $1.82 vs $1.76
items.take: J.B. Hunt reported Q3 operating revenues of $3.68 billion versus $3.05 billion a year earlier, operating income of $247.1 million versus $242.7 million and diluted EPS of $1.82 versus $1.76. Intermodal revenue rose 20% to $1.83 billion while Dedicated operating income fell 22% to $81.7 million. Revenue grew about ten times faster than operating income, so the quarter is a volume story with margins still squeezed.

items.headline: Alcoa Q3 net income rises to $483M, or $1.81 a share; revenue $3.70B
items.take: Alcoa reported Q3 revenue of $3,704 million versus $3,966 million in Q2 and $2,995 million a year earlier, with net income attributable to Alcoa of $483 million, or $1.81 a diluted share, versus $232 million, or $0.88, a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA excluding special items was $789 million, down from $901 million in Q2, and free cash flow was $472 million. The year-over-year gain is large, but the sequential dip in revenue and adjusted EBITDA shows the quarter came off a stronger Q2.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield eases to 5.19% on Oct. 14; 2s10s narrows to 37 bp
items.take: The Fed's H.15 release shows the 10-year constant-maturity Treasury yield at 5.19% on October 14, down from 5.21% on October 13, while the 2-year rose to 4.82% from 4.79%; the 30-year slipped to 5.52% from 5.56%. That narrows the 2-year/10-year spread to 37 basis points from 42. Front-end yields rising as the long end eases is the pattern of a market leaning toward more Fed tightening rather than toward a growth scare.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: 10-year TIPS real yield dips to 2.84%, leaving a 2.35% breakeven
items.take: Per the Fed's H.15, the 10-year inflation-indexed yield fell to 2.84% on October 14 from 2.88% on October 13, against a 5.19% nominal 10-year. That puts the implied 10-year breakeven at 2.35%, up from 2.33% a day earlier. Real yields doing most of the easing while breakevens edge up suggests investors are still adding inflation compensation after this week's price data.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: Interactive Brokers margin loans up 36% to $105.2B; customer credits $186.2B
items.take: Interactive Brokers said customer margin loans increased 36% to $105.2 billion and customer credits rose 20% to $186.2 billion in the third quarter, while customer equity grew 27% to $964.7 billion. Margin borrowing growing faster than client equity is a measure of rising leverage among retail and active traders, a balance worth watching if volatility picks up.

items.headline: J.B. Hunt intermodal loads rise 8% to 585,582 in Q3
items.take: J.B. Hunt's intermodal segment handled 585,582 loads in Q3 versus 539,907 a year earlier, and segment operating income rose 18% to $147.5 million; Integrated Capacity Solutions revenue jumped 57% to $434 million. Rail-intermodal volume growing at a high-single-digit pace is a constructive read on U.S. goods shipping, even as diesel costs pressure trucking margins.

items.headline: Alcoa reaffirms 2026 aluminum output of 2.4–2.6M tonnes after 649 kmt Q3
items.take: Alcoa produced 649,000 metric tons of aluminum and 2,467,000 tons of alumina in Q3, with aluminum shipments of 693,000 tons, and reaffirmed 2026 guidance for 2.4–2.6 million tons of aluminum production and 9.5–9.6 million tons of alumina. It flagged about $30 million of unfavorable raw material and maintenance costs and about $30 million of higher alumina costs in its Q4 aluminum segment. Steady volumes put the onus for Q4 earnings on prices and input costs rather than on production.

items.headline: Interactive Brokers lifts quarterly dividend to $0.15 from $0.0875
items.take: Interactive Brokers declared an increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $0.15 a share from $0.0875, payable December 14, 2026, alongside 35% growth in customer accounts to 5.58 million. A 71% higher payout signals management's confidence that its interest-driven earnings base is durable, though it remains a small share of earnings.

items.headline: Intuit to buy AI revenue-management platform Sequence; terms undisclosed
items.take: Intuit signed an agreement to acquire Sequence, a London- and New York-based platform that automates quote-to-revenue work including pricing, billing, collections and revenue recognition; terms were not disclosed. Sequence will be used to strengthen Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced for mid-market businesses. AlphaGen read: a tuck-in that extends Intuit's push up-market into revenue operations.

items.headline: Sakuu to list via Pyrophyte II SPAC at $600M pre-money equity value
items.take: Sakuu, maker of Kavian dry-printing equipment for battery electrodes, agreed to combine with Pyrophyte Acquisition Corp. II at an implied $600 million pre-money equity value; the combined company is expected to trade on the NYSE as SAKU. Both boards approved the deal, which still needs shareholder votes and an S-4 filing. AlphaGen read: with no PIPE or trust figure disclosed, the cash actually delivered at close is the key unknown.

items.headline: Chubby Group raises $50M at $500M valuation, signs LOI for GEN's 47 U.S. restaurants
items.take: Chubby Group closed a $50 million Series A led by Prysm Capital at a $500 million valuation and signed a letter of intent to take over GEN Restaurant Group's 47 U.S. restaurants and four development sites, valued at up to $100 million and with part of the consideration a note convertible into Chubby equity at a $1.5 billion valuation. The first 12 locations are targeted for November 1, 2026, subject to definitive agreements and approvals. AlphaGen read: the GEN transfer is conditional, so the binding piece today is the equity raise.
items.correction: Clarified that the convertible note is part of the consideration for the GEN assets, not the full payment, per the release.

items.headline: Harmonic Security raises $50M Series B led by Crosspoint
items.take: Harmonic Security raised a $50 million Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners with existing investors participating, taking total funding to $76 million; it has over 90 staff across the US and UK. Proceeds go to engineering and go-to-market expansion. AlphaGen read: AI-usage governance is attracting dedicated security capital.

items.headline: Schwab Q3 revenue rises 17% to a record $7.17B; core net new assets $190.4B
items.take: Charles Schwab reported third-quarter total net revenues of $7.171 billion versus $6.135 billion a year earlier, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.62 against $1.26 and adjusted EPS of $1.69 against $1.31. Net interest revenue rose to $3.476 billion from $3.050 billion, core net new assets reached $190.4 billion and total client assets stood at $13.33 trillion. A 52.7% GAAP pre-tax margin shows asset gathering and spread income compounding together, which leaves the bigger sensitivity in how client cash behaves if rates stay above 5% at the long end.
items.correction: Source link changed from a third-party repost (stockhouse.com) to Schwab's own earnings release; figures unchanged.

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate holds at 7.40%; 15-year eases to 6.71%
items.take: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed rate at 7.40% this week, unchanged from a week earlier and up from 6.27% a year ago; the 15-year averaged 6.71%, down from 6.73%. That leaves the 30-year 113 basis points above its year-ago level. A pause near 7.4% is not relief: with the 10-year Treasury yield still above 5%, financing costs remain the main brake on home purchases heading into the fall.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey

items.headline: Recursion prices $200M stock sale at $3.25 a share; Sanofi options first candidate
items.take: Recursion's Oct. 15 8-K says it agreed to sell 61.54 million shares at $3.25 each for about $200 million in gross proceeds, and put preliminary Sept. 30 cash, equivalents and restricted cash at about $561 million, which it expects, with the offering, to fund operations into 2029. Sanofi optioned the first development candidate from their collaboration, triggering a $10 million milestone, and Recursion reported that 87% of 16 efficacy-evaluable patients in its REC-4881 trial had reduced polyp burden. The raise buys runway into 2029, but at the cost of dilution priced at a low per-share level.

items.headline: Euro slips to $1.1193 on Oct. 9 as the Fed's broad dollar index firms
items.take: Federal Reserve H.10 data on FRED put the euro at $1.1193 on Oct. 9, down from $1.1262 on Oct. 6, while the Fed's nominal broad dollar index rose to 121.60 from 120.90 over the same days. Both series were last updated Oct. 13. With the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.21% on Oct. 13 per FRED, rate differentials remain a support for the dollar against the euro for now.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve H.10 via FRED (DEXUSEU, DTWEXBGS)

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to buy $330M of new Bending Spoons shares, lifting stake to 4%
items.take: Bending Spoons will issue 10 million new ordinary shares to Berkshire Hathaway at $33.00 per share, a $330 million private placement subject to customary closing conditions, after Berkshire invested $600 million at the July 2026 IPO. Berkshire's total ownership rises to 4%. The company framed the cash as added flexibility for acquisitions, which makes this fuel for its roll-up strategy as much as a vote of confidence.

items.headline: ICON raises $200M Series D co-led by Baillie Gifford and BlackRock funds
items.take: ICON raised a $200 million Series D co-led by Baillie Gifford and funds managed by BlackRock, with Tiger Global and Norwest among participants. The 3D-printed construction company says it is on pace for 4x revenue growth in 2026, has built more than 270 homes and structures, and its ICON Prime unit has received more than $370 million in government contracts. Crossover leads point to a company being set up for a later public listing.
items.correction: Corrected '270 printed buildings' to 'more than 270 homes and structures' and attributed the $370 million in government contracts to ICON Prime, per the release.

items.headline: Soufflé Therapeutics closes $135M Series B led by Juvia Group
items.take: Soufflé Therapeutics closed an oversubscribed $135 million Series B led by Juvia Group, adding TCG Crossover, BB Biotech, Fidelity and Balyasny as new investors. Proceeds fund first clinical studies in FSHD, heart failure and a muscle and metabolic program. Crossover participation at Series B usually signals an eventual IPO path once clinical data arrive.

items.headline: FMC cuts Q3 revenue view to $65M–$125M on price cuts to channel inventory
items.take: FMC now expects third-quarter revenue of $65 million to $125 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $565 million to negative $510 million, versus July guidance of $840 million to $900 million (ex-India) and $120 million to $140 million. The cut includes a $625 million to $675 million hit from lowering prices on FMC products held by channel customers in Brazil, Argentina, the U.S. and Canada, and the company flagged a possible material non-cash intangible impairment. This is a deliberate reset of the channel to post-patent, generic-era pricing, and the covenant talks it plans with banks make the balance sheet the next thing to watch.

items.headline: Empire State factory index jumps to 25.5 in October from 7.6
items.take: The New York Fed's general business conditions index rose 17.9 points to 25.5 in October, and new orders climbed to 23.2 from 2.0. Prices paid eased to 59.5 from 63.1, while the six-month outlook index fell to 21.0 from 29.0. Current activity is strong but firms are less upbeat about the months ahead, and input-price pressure remains elevated even after the slight dip.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Empire State Manufacturing Survey via FRED (GACDISA066MSFRBNY)

items.headline: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index falls to 20.9 in October from 37.8
items.take: The Philadelphia Fed's current general activity diffusion index fell 16.9 points to 20.9 in October, after 37.8 in September and 47.4 in August. The reading is still well above zero, so the region's manufacturing activity is growing, just at a slower pace. Paired with the Empire jump, the regional surveys point to a factory sector that is still expanding but uneven, not one that is breaking under energy costs.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey via FRED (GACDFSA066MSFRBPHI)

items.headline: Corteva appeals court order that would bar dividends and buybacks after split
items.take: Corteva said 15 states and one sovereign sued on Oct. 1 to challenge its separation from Vylor, and a federal court in Indiana issued a temporary restraining order on Oct. 9 barring dividends, buybacks and asset disposals outside the ordinary course. The court stayed the order on Oct. 10 pending an emergency motion at the Seventh Circuit, relying on Corteva's statement that it does not intend to declare dividends or repurchase shares while that motion is pending. The completed split is not unwound, but capital returns are effectively frozen until the appeal is decided.

items.headline: Ramp raises $1.85B led by Dragoneer at a $60B valuation
items.take: Ramp's $1.85 billion primary round was led by Dragoneer Investment Group, with Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir Growth co-leading, at a $60 billion valuation; the company reported more than $2 billion in annualized revenue, positive cash flow and over 85,000 customers. Ramp said it has now raised about $5 billion in total equity. Pricing a private fintech at this scale with public-market mutual funds in the book keeps the IPO question open without forcing it.

items.headline: Labcorp to buy BioReference Health assets from OPKO for $722M plus up to $150M earnout
items.take: Labcorp agreed to buy select BioReference Health assets from OPKO Health for $722 million in cash at closing, subject to adjustment, plus an earnout of up to $150 million tied to 4Kscore Test revenue, and expects about $250 million of revenue in the first year after closing. The deal requires regulatory approvals. Tying $150 million to one proprietary test's revenue keeps part of the price contingent on the 4Kscore franchise performing under Labcorp's ownership.
items.correction: Changed the $150 million earnout to 'up to $150 million'; the release describes it as a maximum contingent on 4Kscore Test revenue.

items.headline: Modal raises $750M Series D led by Accel at $15.75B post-money valuation
items.take: Modal raised a $750 million Series D led by Accel, with Kleiner Perkins joining and all existing investors participating, at a $15.75 billion post-money valuation. The company said it crossed $1 billion in annualized run rate and that its sandboxes product alone is at $300 million. Investors are paying up for the infrastructure layer that runs AI models and agents in production, not just the model makers.

items.headline: OrbiMed raises $3B across Private Investments X and Asia Partners VI funds
items.take: OrbiMed raised $3 billion in commitments: more than $1.9 billion for OrbiMed Private Investments X, focused on U.S. and European life sciences venture capital, and more than $1 billion for OrbiMed Asia Partners VI, focused on Asian healthcare growth and venture. Fresh specialist capital of this size adds a sizable pool of money for private biotech, medtech and healthcare services rounds.

items.headline: OMass Therapeutics raises $310M Series C co-led by Bain, Forbion and Novo
items.take: OMass Therapeutics raised an oversubscribed $310 million (£230 million) Series C co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings to take OMS1620 through Phase 2 in congenital adrenal hyperplasia and ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome. Existing backers including Syncona, GV and Sanofi Ventures participated. The size of the round gives OMass capital to reach mid-stage clinical data without returning to investors first for OMS1620.

items.headline: Initial jobless claims edge up to 199,000; four-week average at 198,500
items.take: Seasonally adjusted initial claims rose 1,000 to 199,000 in the week ending Oct. 10, the Labor Department said, and the four-week average rose 250 to 198,500. Insured unemployment fell 4,000 to 1,710,000 for the week ending Oct. 3, with the rate steady at 1.1%. Layoffs remain scarce even as energy costs climb, so the labor market is not yet giving the Fed a reason to look past the inflation side.
items.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor, Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims (Oct. 15, 2026)

items.headline: UnitedHealth Q3 EPS rises to $4.56 as medical care ratio falls to 88.4%
items.take: UnitedHealth reported Q3 revenues of $112.69 billion versus $113.16 billion a year earlier, diluted EPS of $4.56 versus $2.59, and adjusted EPS of $4.69 versus $2.92, released Oct. 13. The medical care ratio fell to 88.4% from 89.9%, UnitedHealthcare served 48.3 million people versus 50.1 million, and the company raised its 2026 outlook to at least $19.50 of EPS and at least $20.50 adjusted. Earnings are recovering on pricing and cost discipline rather than growth, with fewer members and slightly lower revenue.

items.headline: Prologis Q3 core FFO rises to $1.60 a share; leases signed hit 60M square feet
items.take: Prologis reported Q3 revenues of $2.39 billion versus $2.21 billion a year earlier, EPS of $0.86 versus $0.82, and core FFO of $1.60 per share versus $1.49. Average occupancy was 95.1% and net effective rent change on its share of leases was 38.0%; it narrowed 2026 core FFO guidance to $6.25–$6.29 from $6.22–$6.30 while cutting net EPS guidance to $4.05–$4.15 from $4.40–$4.55. The lifted midpoint on core FFO signals warehouse demand is holding up despite the energy shock.

items.headline: Prologis CEO: customers 'running lean on inventory' as excess space clears
items.take: Prologis CEO Daniel S. Letter said "Customers are running lean on inventory, and excess capacity within their networks has largely cleared," citing demand from e-commerce, advanced manufacturing and the data center supply chain. Owned-and-managed period-end occupancy was 95.6% versus a 95.1% quarterly average. Lean inventories plus cleared slack is the setup in which a demand pickup feeds quickly into logistics rents.

items.headline: ManpowerGroup Q3 revenue up 5.2% in constant currency; Q4 EPS guided $1.03–$1.13
items.take: ManpowerGroup reported Q3 revenues of $4.84 billion versus $4.63 billion a year earlier, up 5.2% in constant currency, and diluted EPS of $0.71 versus $0.38; adjusted EPS was $1.01. It guided Q4 diluted EPS to $1.03–$1.13, and CEO Jonas Prising cited "improving demand." Staffing revenue is an early-cycle labor signal, and growth here squares with low jobless claims.

items.headline: September PPI jumps 1.3%, the largest monthly gain since March 2022
items.take: BLS says the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 1.3% in September, seasonally adjusted, after a 0.5% gain in August, and was up 6.3% from a year earlier on an unadjusted basis. Final demand energy jumped 10.8%, and gasoline, up 20.3%, accounted for half of the 2.6% rise in goods prices. The energy shock is now as visible at the producer level as it was in Wednesday's CPI, which makes a quick fade in headline inflation harder to count on.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index news release (September 2026)

items.headline: PPI ex food, energy and trade up 5.0% on the year; raw inputs up 21.5%
items.take: Final demand prices less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% in September and 5.0% over 12 months. Further back in the pipeline, intermediate processed goods rose 2.5% on the month and 14.1% on the year, and unprocessed goods 8.4% and 21.5%. With upstream costs rising this fast against 2.6% core CPI, the open question is how long margins can keep absorbing the gap.
items.source_name: BLS, Producer Price Index news release (September 2026)
items.correction: Removed the unverified claim that the August 12-month rate for final demand less foods, energy and trade services was 4.8%; BLS first reported 4.7% for August.

items.headline: China's producer prices rise 5.0% on the year in September; CPI up 0.9%
items.take: China's National Bureau of Statistics says producer prices rose 5.0% from a year earlier in September and 1.2% from August, versus 3.8% and 0.4% in August, with petroleum extraction prices up 14.5% on the month. Consumer prices rose 0.9% year on year, with core CPI at 1.0% and food down 1.7%. Factory-gate inflation running more than five times consumer inflation points to a margin squeeze for Chinese manufacturers rather than strong domestic demand.
items.source_name: National Bureau of Statistics of China, PPI release (September 2026)
items.correction: Removed an unverified figure of a 14.9% rise in transport fuel prices, which could not be confirmed in NBS data.

items.headline: Euro area industrial output falls 0.5% in August; July revised to a 0.3% drop
items.take: Eurostat says euro area industrial production fell 0.5% in August from July and 1.1% from a year earlier, with July's monthly change revised to -0.3% from -0.1%. Non-durable consumer goods fell 2.7% and intermediate goods 0.8%, while capital goods rose 0.4%. Two straight monthly declines, with intermediate goods also down, suggest higher energy costs are weighing on European industry.
items.correction: Corrected the description of August's decline: non-durable consumer goods (-2.7%), not intermediate goods (-0.8%), fell most.

items.headline: CCC Intelligent Solutions to be acquired by GTCR-led group with Elliott for $6.1B
items.take: CCC agreed to be acquired for $7.75 per share in cash by a consortium led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management, an enterprise value of about $6.1 billion and about a 44% premium to the unaffected July 9 close. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals, with no financing condition. Elliott joining as a buyer rather than an agitator is the notable structural detail in this software take-private.

items.headline: EQT to buy U.S. real estate manager Stockbridge for $375M plus up to $175M earnout
items.take: EQT will pay a $375 million cash base from its balance sheet for Stockbridge, which has about $16.5 billion of fee-generating AUM, plus up to $175 million over 2027–2030 tied to new-product fundraising. Stockbridge is projected to generate about $35–45 million of fee-related EBITDA in 2027, with closing expected in Q1 2027. The deal adds to the run of alternative managers buying their way into U.S. real estate platforms.
items.correction: Reworded the attribution of the $35–45 million 2027 fee-related EBITDA projection, which is described as Stockbridge's projection.

items.headline: Agilent to buy digital pathology software firm Proscia for $240M plus up to $30M
items.take: Agilent agreed to acquire Proscia in an all-cash deal valued at $240 million at closing plus up to $30 million in milestones, expected to close early in Agilent's fiscal 2027. Proscia reports trailing twelve-month revenue above $18 million and FDA 510(k) clearance for primary diagnosis. The price signals Agilent paying up for software to sit alongside its pathology instruments.

items.headline: Labelbox raises more than $100M Series E led by Infinitum Partners
items.take: Labelbox raised more than $100 million in Series E financing, including equity and a credit facility, led by Infinitum Partners with Wipro Ventures, a16z and B Capital participating. The press release disclosed no valuation or equity/debt split. The mix of debt in the headline figure makes it a less clean read on AI-data valuations than a pure equity round.
items.correction: Clarified that the press release, not Labelbox overall, omitted a valuation; the company's blog cited a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation.

items.headline: September retail sales rise 0.8%; August revised up to a 1.3% gain
items.take: Census estimates September retail and food services sales at $745.0 billion, up 0.8% (±0.4%) from August and 6.3% (±0.5%) from September 2025, with the July-to-August gain revised to 1.3% from 1.1%. Sales for July through September were up 5.5% from a year earlier. Two strong nominal months are partly a price story in an energy shock, so the volume read will depend on how much of the gain came at the pump.
items.source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, Advance Monthly Retail Trade (September 2026)

items.headline: Marsh Q3 revenue rises 8% to $6.86B; adjusted EPS up 10% to $2.03
items.take: Marsh reported third-quarter revenue of $6.863 billion versus $6.351 billion a year earlier, with 5% underlying growth, and GAAP EPS of $1.69 versus $1.51. Consulting revenue grew 9% (8% underlying) while Risk & Insurance Services grew 7% (3% underlying). The gap between the two segments is the signal: broking growth has cooled, and consulting is doing more of the lifting.

items.headline: High-yield spread at 3.16%, 56bp above its August low; IG flat at 0.83%
items.take: The ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread was 3.16% on October 13, versus a 2026 low of 2.60% on August 28 and 2.83% on January 2. The investment-grade spread was 0.83%, against 0.79% on January 2. Widening concentrated in junk rather than high-grade credit is consistent with an energy shock hitting weaker balance sheets first.

items.headline: Treasury to announce 20-year reopening and new 5-year TIPS today
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists today's announcement of a 20-year bond reopening for auction on October 21 and a 5-year TIPS for October 22, alongside today's 4-week and 8-week bill auctions. The 2-, 5- and 7-year notes and 2-year FRN follow the week of October 26. With the 30-year at 5.56% on October 13 per the Fed's H.15, demand at the long end next week is a live test.

items.headline: Bowman: SVB review found Fed staff saw risks months before failure
items.take: In an October 14 speech in Bangkok, Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said preliminary findings of an independent review show Fed staff knew of SVB's interest rate and liquidity risk at least nine months before its receivership, with unclear decision rights delaying action. She said the Fed is weighing clearer responsibilities between the Board and Reserve Banks and direct escalation paths for examiners. The direction is fewer, sharper findings focused on core financial risk, which would change how banks experience supervision rather than its intensity.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman

items.headline: Penske Automotive to be taken private by Penske Corp. and Mitsui at $212 a share
items.take: Penske Automotive agreed to be acquired by a buyer owned by Penske Corporation and Mitsui for $212.00 per share in cash, valuing the company at an enterprise value of about $16.3 billion. Penske is expected to own about 64% and Mitsui 36% after closing, expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and a majority vote of unaffiliated stockholders. The majority-of-the-minority condition is the key protection for public holders in a buyout led by the controlling shareholder.

items.headline: Alaunos completes Velaris Therapeutics acquisition alongside $350M private placement
items.take: Alaunos Therapeutics completed its acquisition of PAH drug developer Velaris Therapeutics alongside a private placement of convertible preferred stock raising about $350 million, led by Fairmount with Venrock, T. Rowe Price-advised accounts, Wellington and Janus Henderson participating. Purchase terms were not disclosed, and the company expects its funding to last into 2029. The deal effectively recapitalizes Alaunos around Velaris's ActRII-targeted pipeline.

items.headline: TSMC Q3 revenue up 50.9% to NT$1.49T; Q4 guided to $52.3B–$54.3B
items.take: TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion (US$46.72 billion), up 50.9% from a year earlier in NT$ terms, with net income and diluted EPS both up 68.7% to NT$763.06 billion and NT$29.43 (US$4.60 per ADR unit); gross margin was 66.4% and 3nm and 5nm made up 33% and 28% of wafer revenue. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion with a 65%–67% gross margin. The guide's midpoint implies roughly 14% sequential growth in dollar terms, the clearest read yet that leading-edge demand, including the 2nm ramp, is still growing strongly.
items.correction: Clarified that 50.9% growth is in NT$ terms and replaced 'still accelerating' since the Q4 guide midpoint (+14.1% q/q) is below Q3's 16.2% q/q US$ growth.

items.headline: Beige Book: 'Higher oil prices permeated all District reports'
items.take: The Fed's October Beige Book, based on information collected through Oct. 5, says two of 12 Districts reported moderate growth, three modest, four slight and three no significant change; four Districts said the pace of price increases picked up, three called price growth robust and eight moderate. Labor markets were little changed and most Districts saw flat or slightly lower consumer spending, with over half noting it was driven by high-income households. Ahead of the Oct. 27–28 FOMC, the mix of soft demand and broadening energy pass-through is the stagflation-tinged picture the committee has to weigh.

items.headline: PNC Q3 EPS rises to $4.97 as net interest income climbs 15%
items.take: PNC earned $2.10 billion, or $4.97 a diluted share, in the third quarter versus $1.82 billion and $4.35 a year earlier; adjusted EPS was $5.09 excluding FirstBank integration costs and net significant items. Revenue rose 11% from a year earlier to $6.56 billion on net interest income of $4.21 billion, up 15%, while net loan charge-offs rose to $257 million from $179 million. Spread income is doing the work as fee revenue cooled from the second quarter, and the release's own planning assumption of two more Fed hikes suggests that tailwind has further to run.
items.source_name: PNC Financial Services Group, Q3 2026 earnings release

items.headline: U.S. Bancorp Q3 EPS rises to $1.34 on 13% noninterest income growth
items.take: U.S. Bancorp's third-quarter net income rose to $2.20 billion, or $1.34 a diluted share, from $2.00 billion and $1.22, on taxable-equivalent net revenue of $7.97 billion versus $7.33 billion. Noninterest income rose 13.1% to $3.48 billion and net interest income 5.6% to $4.49 billion, while the efficiency ratio improved to 55.9% from 57.2%. Fee growth outpacing spread income is the notable split here, though no buybacks in the quarter shows capital is still being conserved.

items.headline: BNY Q3 EPS rises 24% to $2.34; custody and administration assets hit $63.4T
items.take: BNY reported third-quarter revenue of $5.68 billion, up 12%, and diluted EPS of $2.34 versus $1.88, with fee revenue up 12% to $4.08 billion and net interest income up 15% to $1.42 billion. Assets under custody and/or administration reached $63.4 trillion, and the bank returned $1.4 billion to shareholders. A 38.5% pre-tax margin and 29.0% return on tangible common equity show operating leverage in the custody model, extending the pattern State Street showed a day earlier.

items.headline: U.S. Bancorp provision rises to $654M, including $135M for an acquired card book
items.take: U.S. Bancorp's third-quarter provision for credit losses was $654 million versus $571 million a year earlier, including a $135 million initial provision tied to loans acquired in its small business credit card portfolio purchase. The net charge-off ratio improved to 0.51% from 0.56%. Stripping out the purchase accounting, underlying loss content looks stable rather than deteriorating, which matters more for credit sentiment than the headline provision.

items.headline: Waller: policy to focus on the inflation side 'for at least the near term'
items.take: In an Oct. 8 speech, Governor Waller noted the FOMC raised its policy rate 25 basis points in September to 3.75%–4%, and that 16 of the 18 participants who submitted dots anticipated at least one more hike; he said the hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings. He cited a 3% 12-month core PCE inflation rate. The framing keeps an October move live but signals the committee would rather pace tightening than pre-commit, which leaves incoming data such as the Beige Book's energy pass-through doing the deciding.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, Governor Waller speech, Oct. 8, 2026

items.headline: Australia's jobless rate at 4.7% in September as employment falls 39,300
items.take: Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose 0.1 point on unrounded estimates to 4.7% in September, employment fell by 39,300, and the participation rate slipped to 66.8% from 67.0%, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. A falling job count alongside lower participation points to genuine cooling rather than a surge in job seekers, which complicates any tightening bias from the Reserve Bank of Australia.
items.source_name: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force, Australia, September 2026

items.headline: Ericsson Q3 organic sales up 7%; flags component costs as a 2027 margin headwind
items.take: Ericsson reported third-quarter net sales of SEK 59.5 billion versus SEK 56.2 billion, with organic growth of 7% driven by Networks, and diluted EPS of SEK 1.77 versus SEK 3.33, which included a SEK 1.72 per share divestment gain. Adjusted gross margin was 47.7% versus 48.1%, and the company said component costs are a headwind to gross margin next year. Organic growth is back, but the warning on input costs suggests the margin story will be harder to sustain in 2027 than the sales story.
items.source_name: Ericsson Q3 2026 report (company release via PR Newswire)

items.headline: Fed survey: real median family net worth rose 2% from 2022 to $215,900
items.take: The Fed's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances found real median net worth rose 2% between 2022 and 2025 to $215,900 and real mean net worth 7% to $1.24 million, while real median family income rose 7% to $82,200 and the real mean fell 6%. The share of families with debt payments above 40% of income rose to 8.6% from 6.5%, a level last seen in the 2013 survey. A rising share of heavily burdened borrowers alongside flat median wealth gives the Fed a more fragile household backdrop to tighten into than the averages suggest.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances release

items.headline: SEC proposes crypto custody framework for advisers and funds, including self-custody
items.take: The SEC proposed a tailored framework for how registered investment advisers and regulated funds can custody crypto assets, including allowing self-custody in certain circumstances and letting state trust companies serve as custodians; comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication. Chairman Atkins said the plan would 'provide a clear regulatory framework for the custody of crypto assets.' Clear custody rules are a precondition for wider adviser and fund allocations, making this a structural rather than headline-driven development for crypto access.

items.headline: Rocket Lab now expects Neutron's inaugural launch in 2027
items.take: Rocket Lab said after the close on Oct. 14 that the inaugural launch of its Neutron rocket is now expected to occur in 2027 under an adjusted schedule. The release did not give a reason or quantify any financial impact, pointing instead to an investor presentation. The slip pushes out one of the company's most closely watched development milestones, and the lack of a stated reason puts the burden on the accompanying investor presentation.
items.source_name: Rocket Lab investor relations release, Oct. 14, 2026

items.headline: J&J Q3 sales rise 5.9% to $25.4B; 2026 sales guidance raised to $101.2B midpoint
items.take: Johnson & Johnson reported third-quarter sales of $25.40 billion, up 5.9% from $23.99 billion, with Innovative Medicine up 7.7% to $16.76 billion and MedTech up 2.5% to $8.64 billion. Diluted EPS fell to $0.09 from $2.12, reflecting special items including a one-time charge for its proposed talc litigation resolution, while adjusted EPS was $2.59 versus $2.80; the company raised 2026 guidance to $101.0 billion to $101.4 billion of sales and $11.05 to $11.15 of adjusted EPS. Pharma is still doing the heavy lifting, and the gap between reported and adjusted earnings shows how much of the quarter's story is the litigation charge rather than operations.

items.headline: Fannie Mae now sees 30-year mortgage rates averaging 7.5% in 2027, up from 6.7%
items.take: Fannie Mae's October 12 housing forecast puts the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.4% in 4Q26 and 7.5% for 2027, versus 6.8% and 6.7% in its September 11 forecast. It cut its 2027 total home sales forecast to 4.713 million from 4.882 million and existing-home sales to 4.061 million from 4.215 million. A forecaster that a month ago expected rates to level off near 6.7% now expects them to climb further, which pushes any housing turnover recovery out past next year.
items.source_name: Fannie Mae ESR Housing Forecast, October 2026
items.correction: Fannie Mae's September forecast had rates rising to 6.8% in 4Q26 then holding at 6.7%, not drifting lower; wording corrected.

items.headline: EIA: U.S. diesel averages $6.18 a gallon, up $2.51 from a year ago
items.take: EIA's October 14 update put the U.S. average on-highway diesel price at $6.179 a gallon for the week of Oct. 12, down 2.0 cents on the week but $2.514 above a year ago, while regular gasoline averaged $4.331, down 2.3 cents and $1.270 higher year over year. California diesel averaged $8.091, up 0.9 cent on the week. By code, diesel is about 69% above year-ago levels against roughly 41% for gasoline, so the energy shock is landing hardest on freight and goods costs.
items.source_name: EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update

items.headline: USDA lifts 2026/27 corn yield to 181.2 bushels; ending stocks raised to 1.85B
items.take: USDA's October WASDE raised its 2026/27 U.S. corn yield forecast to 181.2 bushels an acre from 178.5, lifting production to 16.034 billion bushels from 15.800 billion and ending stocks to 1.849 billion from 1.567 billion. The season-average farm price forecast was cut to $4.70 a bushel from $4.80, while soybean ending stocks rose to 315 million bushels with the price held at $12.00. An 18% jump in projected corn carryout leaves grains as one of the few commodity markets where supply is loosening, in contrast with energy.
items.source_name: USDA World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates, October 2026

items.headline: Domino's Q3 EPS rises to $4.60 as U.S. same-store sales edge up 0.3%
items.take: Domino's Pizza reported third-quarter total revenues of $1.186 billion, up 3.4%, and diluted EPS of $4.60 versus $4.08. U.S. same-store sales grew 0.3% and international same-store sales rose 0.2% excluding currency, with global retail sales up 3.2% ex-FX on 175 net new stores. Growth is coming from new units rather than existing restaurants, which suggests demand at existing restaurants is roughly flat.

items.headline: EIA sees end-October gas storage at 3,850 Bcf, 2% above five-year average
items.take: EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts U.S. working natural gas inventories of 3,850 billion cubic feet at the end of October, 2% above the five-year average, with Henry Hub averaging $3.48 per MMBtu in 2026 and $3.16 in 2027. It projects LNG exports of 17.6 Bcf/d in 2026 and 18.6 Bcf/d in 2027. Comfortable gas storage stands apart from tight oil and diesel, so U.S. natural gas is not adding to this winter's energy inflation pressure.
items.source_name: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, Natural Gas

items.headline: SEC approves exchange listing of binary options tied to company KPIs
items.take: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said on Oct. 13 that the Commission voted to approve an exchange's proposed rule change permitting cash-settled binary options on specified key performance indicators reported by certain stock issuers. He stressed the order speaks solely to these contracts and does not address similar products on the same KPIs. Exchange-listed contracts on reported operating metrics would give investors a regulated way to trade the earnings datapoints themselves, not just the stock.

items.headline: SEC clears Cboe BZX to list 3x bitcoin and ether ETFs from Volatility Shares
items.take: In an Oct. 2 order (Release No. 34-106577), the SEC approved Cboe BZX's rule change to list and trade six VS Trust funds, including a 3x Bitcoin ETF and a 3x Ether ETF, alongside 3x gold, silver, crude oil and natural gas funds. Each seeks three times the daily performance of a futures-based benchmark, and needed a specific approval because the 3x multiple falls outside BZX's generic listing standards. Triple-leveraged crypto funds reset daily, so their returns over longer holding periods can diverge sharply from three times the underlying move.

items.headline: BoE's Bailey: rates 'cannot produce more oil or gas' in a supply shock
items.take: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said in an Oct. 8 speech that a negative supply shock produces weaker output and higher inflation, and that looking through it is possible only if inflation expectations stay well anchored. He said banks remain well capitalized with no funding stress, but warned that leveraged positions can be unwound rapidly. The message is a central bank reserving the right to tighten into an energy shock rather than promising to look past it.
items.source_name: Bank of England, speech by Andrew Bailey

items.headline: STERIS to buy specialty surgical products maker Xodus Medical for $2.1B cash
items.take: STERIS agreed to acquire Xodus Medical for $2.1 billion in cash at closing plus up to $150 million in 2028 earnouts, financed primarily with debt and backed by a bridge commitment of up to $2.0 billion. Closing is expected by December 31, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. The deal deepens STERIS's tilt toward recurring surgical consumables.
items.correction: Headline corrected to describe Xodus Medical as a specialty surgical products maker, as the 8-K states, rather than a surgical safety products maker.

items.headline: Iambic Therapeutics prices $150M Nasdaq IPO at $16 a share
items.take: Iambic Therapeutics priced 9,375,000 shares at $16.00 for $150.0 million in gross proceeds, with Nasdaq trading under IAM expected to start October 15 and closing expected October 16. Underwriters hold a 30-day option on 1,406,250 more shares. The raise gives the clinical-stage company a public-market currency and fresh capital for its pipeline.
items.source_name: Iambic press release (Business Wire, via Stockhouse)

items.headline: Atlas Warehouse Lending prices $750M of 6.25% fixed-to-floating notes due 2032
items.take: Atlas Warehouse Lending Company priced $750 million of senior notes due 2032 at 6.250% fixed to November 2031, then Compounded SOFR plus 2.534%, in a Rule 144A deal expected to close October 21. Proceeds fund assets and general corporate purposes. The print shows steady credit-market demand for warehouse-lending platforms.

items.headline: SSR Mining to buy Roxmore Resources for C$6.75 a share, about $464M equity value
items.take: SSR Mining agreed to buy Roxmore Resources for C$6.75 per share in cash, a fully diluted equity value of about $464 million and enterprise value of $392 million, excluding a SpinCo distributed to Roxmore holders. Closing is expected in Q4 2026. The deal adds the Converse gold project to SSR's long-dated development pipeline.

items.headline: Payward signs deal to buy EU-licensed Saldo Bank; terms undisclosed
items.take: Payward signed a definitive agreement to acquire Saldo Bank, a Lithuania-licensed digital bank with passporting across five European markets; terms were not disclosed and closing is expected in 2027 pending regulatory approvals. An EU banking license would let Payward, whose companies include Kraken, add deposit and lending products in Europe.

items.headline: Mubadala Capital completes ~$6.2B acquisition of Clear Channel Outdoor
items.take: Clear Channel Outdoor said its take-private by Mubadala Capital, a subsidiary of Mubadala Investment Company, is complete in a transaction valued at approximately $6.2 billion, following regulatory and stockholder approvals. Its common stock will be delisted from the NYSE. The close takes a major listed out-of-home advertising operator into sovereign-backed private hands.

items.headline: Medtronic accepts 55.0M shares in exchange for all 252.8M MiniMed shares it held
items.take: Medtronic said 297,521,390 shares were tendered in its MiniMed split-off exchange offer and 55,032,401 accepted at a final proration factor of 18.289133%, in exchange for its entire remaining 252,813,348 MiniMed shares. That implies about 4.59 MiniMed shares per Medtronic share, and Medtronic will retain no MiniMed stock. The heavy oversubscription let Medtronic fully exit MiniMed while shrinking its own share count.

items.headline: Agility to sell Tristar stake to Aegis Logistics at $1.5B enterprise value
items.take: Agility Global agreed to sell its stake in energy-logistics business Tristar to India's Aegis Logistics in a deal valuing Tristar at $1.5 billion enterprise value and $882 million equity value, about 6.0x 2025 EBITDA. Closing is expected before the end of March 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. The purchase gives Aegis a global fuel-logistics network built on $1.4 billion of annual revenue.
items.correction: The release gives Tristar's $1.4 billion revenue as an annual figure without attributing it to 2025; wording corrected.

items.headline: Select Water prices upsized $900M of 7.625% senior notes due 2034
items.take: A Select Water Solutions subsidiary priced $900 million of 7.625% senior notes due November 1, 2034 at par, upsized from $800 million, with closing expected October 21. Proceeds partly fund the cash consideration for Pilot Water Solutions and repay the term loan and revolver borrowings. The upsizing secures long-dated funding for the Pilot deal at a fixed coupon.
items.source_name: Select Water Solutions press release (PR Newswire)

items.headline: JPMorgan Q3 net income rises 6% to $15.3B; EPS $5.57 vs $5.07
items.take: JPMorgan Chase reported third-quarter net income of $15.3 billion, or $5.57 per share, versus $14.4 billion, or $5.07, a year earlier, on reported revenue of $50.2 billion against $46.4 billion. Net interest income rose 13% to $27.1 billion, the provision for credit losses fell to $2.7 billion from $3.4 billion, and net charge-offs dropped $389 million to $2.2 billion. Falling credit costs contrast with the higher provision Wells Fargo reported, though JPMorgan also scaled net buybacks back to $664 million.

items.headline: EIA sees Brent averaging $105 in Q4 after a $114 September
items.take: EIA's October Short-Term Energy Outlook says Brent averaged $114 per barrel in September, $23 above August, and forecasts $105 for 4Q26, $96 for full-year 2026 and $84 for 2027. EIA assumes Middle East oil flows stay constrained through the fourth quarter. The forecast path implies relief in 2027, but it hinges on supply recovering rather than demand cooling, which keeps energy the swing factor for inflation.

items.headline: EIA: Middle East shut-ins eased to 4.8M b/d in September from 10.9M peak
items.take: EIA estimates Middle East shut-in oil production averaged 4.8 million barrels a day in September, down from a peak of 10.9 million b/d in May, and forecasts 4.5 million b/d in 4Q26. It estimates global oil inventories fell by an average of 1.9 million b/d in 3Q26, with a further draw of about 0.7 million b/d expected in 4Q26. Supply is coming back, but inventories are still being drawn, so the market has little cushion if flows disrupt again.

items.headline: 30-year mortgage rate climbs to 7.40%, up 110 bp from a year ago
items.take: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed rate at 7.40% for the week of Oct. 8, up from 7.28% a week earlier and 6.30% a year ago; the 15-year averaged 6.73%. That is a 12 basis point weekly rise and 110 basis points over the year. With the 10-year Treasury above 5%, mortgage rates have little room to ease, which keeps affordability the binding constraint on home sales.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey

items.headline: EIA: East Coast distillate stocks ran 32% below normal in September
items.take: EIA says East Coast distillate inventories were 32% below the five-year seasonal average in September and expects them to stay about 20% below average through winter. It forecasts retail diesel at $5.19 a gallon for 2026, easing to $4.49 in 2027, and says tight global diesel markets are boosting refiners' crude demand. That matches the Dallas Fed's Beige Book report that diesel was the most commonly cited factor driving up costs in its district, a channel that reaches freight and goods prices with a lag.
items.correction: Corrected the Dallas Fed Beige Book reference: diesel was the most commonly cited cost driver, not the top cost driver.

items.headline: Euro area flash inflation rose to 3.8% in September on 18.8% energy
items.take: Eurostat's flash estimate put euro area annual inflation at 3.8% in September, up from 3.2% in August, with energy at 18.8% versus 14.3%. Inflation excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco was estimated at 2.5%, against 2.4% in August, and services rose to 3.2%. As in the U.S., the headline jump is mostly energy, which leaves the ECB weighing a supply shock against a still-contained core.
items.source_name: Eurostat euro indicators, flash estimate September 2026

items.headline: Yen at 158.34 per dollar on Oct. 9, per Fed H.10 data
items.take: The Federal Reserve's H.10 noon buying rate put the dollar at 158.34 yen on Oct. 9, versus 157.97 on Oct. 5, according to the FRED series updated Oct. 13. The dollar edged higher against the yen on three of the four trading days from Oct. 6 to Oct. 9, dipping only on Oct. 7. With U.S. 10-year yields above 5%, the rate gap with Japan continues to favor the dollar, keeping yen weakness a live issue for Japanese policymakers.

items.headline: EIA's weekly petroleum report moves to Thursday, Oct. 15
items.take: EIA says the next Weekly Petroleum Status Report will be released Thursday, Oct. 15, at 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time because of the federal closure on Monday, Oct. 12. EIA has also discontinued the full-report PDF, effective Sept. 23. With distillate stocks already tight, Thursday's inventory figures are the next official read on whether winter fuel supplies are rebuilding.

items.headline: Fairfax named strategic buyer for 60.72% of IDBI Bank at about $5.6B
items.take: India's government declared a Fairfax subsidiary the strategic buyer for a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank at INR 81 a share, about INR 528.78 billion (roughly $5.6 billion), a premium of about 23% to book value. No binding agreements are signed yet, and Fairfax plans to contribute its Digit insurers and Fairfax India's IIFL Capital stake to the bank. The deal still needs Reserve Bank of India, SEBI and, for the Digit piece, insurance-regulator approval.

items.headline: BlackRock's HPS buys WCAS stake, valued near $2.8B, in Humana CenterWell clinics JV
items.take: Funds managed by HPS Investment Partners, part of BlackRock, will buy WCAS's equity in Humana's CenterWell clinic joint ventures, valued at about $2.8 billion, and own a majority of a new JV covering nearly 150 clinics. The new JV drops the put option, and Humana gets the right to buy clinics back starting in 2028. Humana says removing the put should significantly reduce balance-sheet liabilities, while CenterWell keeps managing the clinics.

items.headline: Cipher Digital prices $850M of 0.00% convertible notes due 2032
items.take: Cipher Digital priced $850 million of 0.00% convertible notes due 2032 with a conversion price of about $15.31, a 35% premium, and net proceeds of about $835.1 million before about $89.7 million of capped calls. The cash goes to its Barber Lake project and HPC build-out. Zero-coupon converts remain a common way for AI data-center developers to fund build-outs.

items.headline: Brookdale to buy 30 leased communities from Welltower for $290M
items.take: Brookdale agreed to buy 30 leased communities from Welltower for $290 million, cutting about $17.8 million of 2027 cash rent, and closed a separate $157 million purchase of 17 communities. Its owned share of units rises toward nearly 80% after closing. Buying out leases is how Brookdale is shrinking fixed rent obligations.

items.headline: Citigroup Q3 EPS rises to $2.85 on $23.8B of revenue; NII up 14%
items.take: Citigroup reported third-quarter net income of $5.2 billion, or $2.85 per diluted share, versus $3.8 billion, or $1.86, a year earlier, on revenues of $23.8 billion against $22.1 billion. Net interest income rose 14%, RoTCE was 11.5% and the bank returned $4.1 billion to shareholders with a CET1 ratio of 12.8%. Revenue growing about 8% while reported expenses fell 2% is the operating leverage Citi has been promising, though the prior-year comparison included a Banamex-related goodwill impairment.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield at 5.21% on Oct. 13, down 7 bp from Oct. 7
items.take: The Fed's H.15 release shows the 10-year constant-maturity yield at 5.21% on October 13 versus 5.28% on October 7, while the 30-year eased to 5.56% from 5.67% and the 2-year was little changed at 4.79%. That leaves the 2s10s curve at 42 basis points. The long end is doing the easing while the front end holds, a pattern that points to some relief in term premium rather than a shift in expected policy.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: Citi Q3 provision of $2.6B includes $2.2B of net credit losses
items.take: Citigroup said its third-quarter provision for credit losses was $2.6 billion, reflecting $2.2 billion of net credit losses and a net reserve build of $369 million. The bank cited growth in U.S. Consumer Cards among the drivers of its 14% rise in net interest income. Net credit losses of $2.2 billion are the price of that NII growth, and the modest reserve build suggests the bank sees no sharp turn in consumer credit yet.

items.headline: 3-month Treasury yield sits 38 bp above the effective fed funds rate
items.take: On October 13 the 3-month constant-maturity Treasury yield was 4.26% while the effective federal funds rate was 3.88%, per the Fed's H.15 release; the 2-year yield was 4.79%. The 3-month yield has edged up from 4.22% on October 7. Bills yielding well above overnight policy is consistent with a market that leans toward tighter Fed policy ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: 10-year TIPS real yield at 2.88%, leaving a 2.33% breakeven
items.take: The 10-year inflation-indexed Treasury yield was 2.88% on October 13 versus a 5.21% nominal 10-year yield, per the Fed's H.15, implying a breakeven inflation spread of about 2.33 percentage points. The real yield has eased from 2.92% on October 7. Real yields near 2.9% are doing most of the tightening in financial conditions; inflation compensation remains contained.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve, H.15 Selected Interest Rates

items.headline: SentinelOne prices $1.25B of 0.00% convertible notes due 2031
items.take: SentinelOne priced $1.25 billion of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2031 with an initial conversion price of about $31.21, a 30% premium, and expected net proceeds of about $1,224 million. About $150 million goes to buying back shares and $131.6 million to capped calls. Zero-coupon converts remain a cheap way for software companies to raise cash.

items.headline: IonQ to acquire zero-trust security firm Elisity for up to $1.3B in stock
items.take: IonQ agreed to acquire Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million of earnout, with share count set by a 20-day VWAP collared between $33.07 and $49.61. Closing is expected in Q4 2026. IonQ keeps using its equity to build a security franchise around its quantum business.

items.headline: Bumble agrees to $1.3B all-cash sale to Ithaca Holdings at $6.05 a share
items.take: Ithaca Holdings will acquire Bumble for $6.05 per Class A share in cash, valuing the company at $1.3 billion and about a 138% premium to the October 9 unaffected close. Written consent from Blackstone affiliates and Whitney Wolfe Herd already provides the required shareholder approval. The deal puts the app under a long-term private owner whose co-CEOs will run Bumble.

items.headline: AT&T to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2B cash
items.take: AT&T agreed to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash at closing, plus contractual and contingent benefits, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027. AT&T will report the unit as held for sale in its Q3 10-Q. The exit concentrates AT&T on U.S. fiber and wireless and gives Televisa a mobile network to pair with its fixed broadband.

items.headline: Galderma to buy ZO Skin Health from Blackstone-backed owners for $1.5B
items.take: Galderma agreed to acquire 100% of ZO Skin Health in an all-cash deal at an enterprise value of $1.5 billion, funded with cash on hand and bank loans; ZO had about $330 million of net sales in the twelve months to June 2026. Closing is expected in Q4 2026 or early 2027. The price, roughly 4.5 times sales, shows strategic buyers paying up for scaled professional-channel skincare.

items.headline: Fastenal Q3 sales rise 15.5% to $2.46B; 2026 net capex seen at $310M–$330M
items.take: Fastenal reported third-quarter net sales of $2.46 billion, up 15.5%, with operating margin of 21.5% versus 20.7% and diluted EPS of $0.35, up 19.8%. The company expects 2026 net capital spending of $310 million to $330 million, against $230.6 million in 2025. Double-digit daily sales growth is a useful real-time read on U.S. industrial activity, and the heavier spend is a bet that it lasts.

items.headline: Progressive Q3 premiums written up 4% to $22.3B; combined ratio 88.7
items.take: Progressive reported third-quarter net premiums written of $22.3 billion, up 4%, and a combined ratio of 88.7, versus 89.5 a year earlier. Net income fell 3% to $2.54 billion, or $4.37 a share. Underwriting margins remain strong, but premium growth in the low single digits signals the auto insurance pricing cycle has cooled.

items.headline: Beige Book: Dallas Fed says diesel is the top cost driver in its district
items.take: The Dallas Fed's section of today's Beige Book says price pressures picked up, with diesel the most commonly cited factor driving costs and causing widespread margin compression. Retailers voiced concern, but most said higher diesel had not yet led to price hikes. That pass-through gap is exactly what the FOMC will be watching after September's energy-driven CPI print.

items.headline: Wells Fargo earns $1.87 a share in Q3 as provisions rise to $1.0B
items.take: Wells Fargo reported third-quarter net income of $6.0 billion, or $1.87 per diluted share, versus $1.66 a year earlier, on revenue of $21.9 billion and net interest income of $12.5 billion. The provision for credit losses rose to $1.03 billion from $681 million, partly on a higher allowance for commercial and industrial and auto loans, and the CET1 ratio was an estimated 10.0%. Higher reserves alongside $2.5 billion of buybacks show a bank comfortable returning capital while building cushions.

items.headline: State Street Q3 EPS rises to $3.69 as net interest income climbs 21%
items.take: State Street reported third-quarter diluted EPS of $3.69, up 33%, on total revenue of $4.0 billion, up 13%, with fee revenue up 11% and net interest income up 21%. Assets under custody and/or administration hit a record $59.2 trillion. Fee revenue is still about 78% of the total, so the custody franchise remains a play on market levels and flows more than on rates.

items.headline: BlackRock AUM reaches $15.5T after $205B of Q3 net inflows
items.take: BlackRock ended the third quarter with $15.5 trillion in assets under management, up 15% from a year earlier, after $205 billion of net inflows in the quarter. Revenue rose 19% to $7.75 billion and as-adjusted diluted EPS rose 38% to $15.93. Flows are broad across ETFs, private markets and cash, which keeps organic fee growth less dependent on equity market direction.

items.headline: ASML posts €11.7B Q3 sales, guides Q4 to €14.2B–€15.2B
items.take: ASML reported third-quarter total net sales of €11.7 billion and net income of €5.0 billion at a 57.5% gross margin, and guided fourth-quarter sales of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion. Full-year 2026 sales are now expected at €44 billion to €45 billion, and the company said planned supply for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customer demand. When the lithography bottleneck says it is capacity-constrained two years out, chip-equipment demand is being set by supply, not orders.

items.headline: Bank of America Q3 net income falls to $6.9B on a $1.2B regulatory charge
items.take: Bank of America earned $6.9 billion, or $0.91 per diluted share, in the third quarter, down from $8.3 billion, or $1.04, a year earlier. Results include a $1.2 billion non-tax-deductible charge, or $0.17 a share, to accrue for civil money penalties tied to Bank Secrecy Act consent orders, while net interest income rose 8% to $16.4 billion. The core lending engine is growing; most of the profit decline is a compliance bill, not a credit problem, with provisions roughly flat at $1.3 billion.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley Q3 net revenues rise to $20.3B; EPS $3.03 vs $2.80
items.take: Morgan Stanley reported third-quarter net revenues of $20.3 billion, up from $18.2 billion a year earlier, with net income of $4.9 billion, or $3.03 per diluted share, versus $4.6 billion, or $2.80, and a 22.6% return on tangible common equity. Revenue up roughly 11.6% and EPS up about 8% point to strong capital generation at a major dealer, a supportive backdrop for large-bank senior debt.
items.correction: Corrected Morgan Stanley's year-over-year revenue growth from roughly 11.5% to 11.6% ($20,338M vs $18,224M per the earnings release).

items.headline: September CPI jumps 0.6%, with gasoline doing most of the work
items.take: Headline CPI rose 0.6% in September after 0.4% in August, putting the 12-month rate at 3.7%. BLS says gasoline rose 9.1% on the month and accounted for over half of the increase. This is an energy shock showing up in the headline, and the market is treating it as a policy problem.

items.headline: The gap that matters: headline at 3.7%, core at 2.6%
items.take: Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.3% in September and 2.6% over the past year. Energy is up 20.4% year over year. The question for the Fed is whether energy prices leak into everything else. Shelter, the stickiest piece, rose 0.4% on the month and 3.2% on the year.

items.headline: Fed meets October 27–28 with inflation moving the wrong way
items.take: The FOMC's next two-day meeting is October 27–28, with the press conference on the 28th. Today's CPI gives the committee a hotter headline print to weigh against a calmer core. The Fed also released its Beige Book, its regional read on the economy, at 2:00 p.m. ET today.

items.headline: Goldman posts $18.68B in Q3 revenue and $17.01 a share
items.take: Goldman reported third-quarter net revenues of $18.68 billion and net earnings of $5.29 billion, or $17.01 per diluted share, for an 18.7% annualized return on equity. Global Banking & Markets brought in $13.46 billion, about 72% of the total. Trading and deal desks are carrying the quarter.
